name: Gulf / US–Iran war
value: 3 ships hit in Hormuz 24 Nov; US blockade on
summary: UKMTO reports three ships struck in Hormuz on 24 Nov; Iran threatens retaliation; US blockade of Iranian ports continues
state: UKMTO reported three vessels struck by projectiles in the Strait of Hormuz on the evening of 24 Nov, with all crew accounted for, after a bulk carrier was hit off Khor Fakkan on 23 Nov; Iran's army chief warned on 24 Nov of retaliation for any new strikes on its infrastructure (ABC News). The US says its naval blockade of Iranian ports has run 130 days, and on 25 Nov its UAE mission issued a security alert citing Iranian attacks on US assets in Bahrain and Kuwait (Gulf News). Iran's army chief ordered the strait closed further day by day on 23 Nov (Euronews). Active strikes and shipping attacks keep the Alert.
for_you: Anyone in the Gulf should follow FCDO travel advice and local authority alerts. Shipping, oil and gas flows through Hormuz remain disrupted, which tends to feed through to fuel and freight costs.
rubric_hit: Active strikes between states and attacks on Gulf shipping (3 ships hit in Hormuz 24 Nov) = Alert

sources.title: ABC News (via AOL) — Iran live updates: 3 tankers attacked in Strait of Hormuz, UKMTO says

why: Direct hostilities between Iran and the US or Israel threaten Gulf energy infrastructure, the Strait of Hormuz and the wider region.
drivers: Strikes and retaliation, attacks on shipping and Gulf states, mediation and ceasefire talks, US force posture.

rubric.alert: Active strikes between states, attacks on Gulf energy infrastructure or shipping, or the Strait of Hormuz substantially closed.
rubric.watch: A ceasefire or stalemate with sporadic strikes, or credible threats of renewed strikes.
rubric.normal: No direct state-on-state hostilities; diplomacy active.
